public_rationale: Ars Technica reported on June 16, 2026 that OpenAI's 2025 net loss was nearly $39 billion, including a large nonrecurring accounting charge [e2]. This supports the OpenAI loss component [e2]. Epoch AI reported on February 4, 2026 that Anthropic projected a $5.2 billion EBITDA loss for 2025; this does not establish final net losses [e3]. CNBC reported on February 20, 2026 that OpenAI's 2025 revenue was $13.1 billion and cash burn was $8 billion [e1]. The supplied reports do not identify the earlier reports being challenged or establish comparable revenue and spending discrepancies of at least $2 billion each [e1, e2]. The evidence therefore leaves the compound claim unresolved [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: The evidence does not identify a definitive earlier baseline for either claimed OpenAI discrepancy [e1, e2].
Cash burn and accounting expenses are different measures; the packet does not reconcile them [e1, e2].
Anthropic's projected EBITDA loss does not establish its final 2025 net loss [e3].
Ars Technica provides secondary reporting on financial statements; the underlying statements and Financial Times verification were not directly inspected for this packet.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI and Anthropic both lose billions of dollars, and OpenAI made billions less and spent billions more in 2025 than reported.

statement.excerpt: They report that Anthropic hit $19 billion in annualized revenue and OpenAI hit $25 billion in annualized revenue — which has been confirmed to refer to a 4-week-long period of revenue multiplied by 12 — as proof that the AI bubble is real, ignoring the fact that both companies lose billions of dollars and that my own reporting says that OpenAI made billions less and spent billions more in 2025.

from_speaker: both companies lose billions of dollars
our_interpretation: Assess the supplied proposition about losses and discrepancies, rather than the surrounding annualized-revenue figures.
Use calendar 2025 for the explicit annual comparison and the latest completed annual period for the ongoing loss assertion.
Read billions as a difference of at least $2 billion, separately for revenue and spending.
The comparison requires an identifiable earlier report measuring the same annual revenue and spending.

The financial figures are reporting-based estimates. The speaker does not specify whether losses mean net losses, operating losses or cash burn; the ordinary net-loss reading must not be populated with another measure.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable records establish multibillion-dollar annual losses at both companies and show OpenAI’s 2025 revenue at least $2 billion below, and spending at least $2 billion above, the identified earlier reports.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish that either company did not have multibillion-dollar losses, or that either claimed OpenAI discrepancy was absent or below $2 billion.
